not_recommended: A JIT inside the CPython process (ORC through libLLVM's C API from ctypes, or llvmlite): it works, but it costs a 117-123 MB libLLVM or a 56 MiB wheel, relies on an ORC C API whose header says it is unstable, needs libgcc_s preloaded RTLD_GLOBAL, and takes 23 ms to compile plus 735 ms when the runtime is bitcode, against a 0.4 ms import of an AOT .so. A later dev loop should be an import hook that runs `pystachy ext` (0.47 s) and caches the result.

Reusing runtime mode's bare `def f(...) -> T: ...` in user code without a marker: today it compiles to a RuntimeError ('ended without returning a value') and CPython returns None, so it would silently change what existing programs mean and break the oracle.

Native `__thread` state in runtime.c, as spike_ext's runtime_lib.diff has it: this resolves a stage-1 disagreement. The driver builds runtime.o with -fPIC; with any `__thread` variable in it, lli-18 fails with 'Unsupported x86-64 relocation type R_X86_64_TLSLD' and cannot materialise the object, even when only an unrelated function is called. spike_ext's own runtime object made hello-world fail under lli while the stock runtime printed 'hi' (SCRATCH/stage2/minimal/t/tls). spike_ext's '40/40 identical' result covered AOT only. -femulated-tls does work.

Pins, handle tables, finalizer queues and parked spans in v1 (web-gc's 150-300 lines): when only scalars and copied str cross, nothing Pystachy allocates is held by a foreign heap, and the single-thread rule makes parking unnecessary. The prototype's 24 runtime.c lines passed every GC-stress case, including nested re-entry.

A C shim for embedding (spike-pys-to-py's pyshim.c) or for CPython's static-inline API: every operation needed is an exported stable-ABI function, which the IR calls through @extern, so the same lib/pyobj.py works in JIT, AOT and inside ext modules.

Version-specific extensions built with Python.h and inlined refcounts: they need headers at build time and one .so per CPython version. The boundary copies scalars and str, so the Limited API's cost (about 5-20% on object-heavy code, per Cython) barely applies.
abi3t-only as the first target: it serves only 3.15+, final since 2026-10-09, and was verified only on 3.15.0b4. It belongs in stage 4, after abi3 3.12.

typed-ir.md §7.4's third lowering now (containers as PyObjects, refcounts derived from liveness): it is blocked on typed-IR step 16 and recoverable elaboration, and it re-baselines the compiler's own IR. The wrapper approach reuses the existing lowering unchanged and can be replaced later.

A shared libpystachy runtime .so: it loses LTO inlining, the runtime calls pys_obj_eq/cmp/repr that each program defines (that broke spike-pys-to-py's runtime.so), and PYS_EXC would be shared between modules. Instead, each extension carries its own internalised runtime.
Header importers (libclang, translate-c, bindgen) inside the compiler: a second toolchain, which the docs reject; Zig moved translate-c out of the language.

Structs by value, varargs and C callbacks in @extern v1: LLVM IR does not lower the C ABI, and llvm/lib/ABI has no C API (LLVM 23 has only x86-64 SysV and BPF, behind a flag). Write a clang-compiled C shim with scalar wrappers instead.
HPy or PyNI as the CPython ABI: HPy declared itself unmaintained in September 2026, and PyNI is a draft with no PEP number.
CPython calling Pystachy through ctypes and a plain shared library: about 250 ns per call against about 24-47 ns, with no conversions and no exception mapping.

Running the raw-C-API bridge under CPython through ctypes.pythonapi as its own oracle: CDLL releases the GIL, and PyDLL raises before the bridge can check for NULL, so its behaviour would diverge. A separate plain-Python twin is simpler and exact.
risks: Name collision: builtin modules come before the program's directory and lib/, so a user's own ffi.py would be shadowed by the builtin `ffi` (none exists in the corpus).
pyobj is deliberately small and verbose (attr/call/of_int), and needs explicit close() until S5. Each Object never closed keeps one Python reference until exit.
The exception mapping loses subclass identity: JSONDecodeError arrives as ValueError. The twin mirrors this, so differential tests pass, but code ported from CPython sees the builtin class.

str length deviation leaks into C calls: passing len(s) to C as a byte count gives different results from CPython for non-ASCII text. Measured: adler32 of 'héllo' was 192152348 in Pystachy and 139985581 in CPython. Mitigate with ffi.nbytes (S4) and docs.

C ABI coverage: only i64, double, ptr and i32 signext were verified, on x86-64 Linux. Expected to hold on AArch64 Linux. macOS needs `-undefined dynamic_lookup` for ext. Windows (python3.dll, SEH instead of Itanium unwinding) is out of scope.
Library names in @extern are platform sonames, such as libz.so.1. They are passed verbatim to dlopen, the linker and ctypes, so source files are not portable across platforms.

Extension restrictions: GIL builds only until S4; calls only from the importing thread; compiled code never releases the GIL, so long calls block other Python threads and delay Ctrl-C; oom, stack overflow and a raising user __str__ during conversion still kill the host process.
Re-importing an ext module runs its top-level code again against process-wide globals that the old module object also sees.
PEP 793/803/820 details (needed for S4) were checked only against 3.15.0b4, not the 3.15.0 final released 2026-10-09.

Embedding depends on finding the right libpython (PYSTACHY_LIBPYTHON, plus PYTHONHOME for relocatable builds such as python-build-standalone). Python is never finalized, so Python atexit handlers do not run unless the program calls pyobj.finalize().

check_runtime.py has to learn that the indirect out_hook call only reads its arguments. Without that it reports file.writelines as writing lists (wL). The alternative, adding wL to RUNTIME, would change IR for programs that call writelines.

@extern calls carry every effect letter (FXALL), so the listget and dictfuse optimizations stop at them. FFI-heavy loops lose those optimizations unless a later, checked `pure=` flag narrows the effects.
The new tests need libpython and python3, so they must stay in a separate, skippable verify step to keep the Python-free CI stage intact.

title: Pystachy FFI: typed `ffi` stubs with a CPython twin, an abi3t/abi3 extension mode, and a small library mode in runtime.c. Pystachy→C and Pystachy→CPython use both tiers; CPython→Pystachy is AOT only, with compile-on-import.
thesis:
Use one declaration form and one boundary layer for all three directions.

**(1) Pystachy calls C or CPython.** Programs declare foreign functions as typed, decorated stubs from a new builtin module `ffi`:
- `@extern("z") def crc32(crc: int, buf: bytes, n: c_uint) -> int: ...` for C;
- `@pycall("json") def dumps(obj: dict[str, int]) -> str: ...` for CPython functions.

This generalizes the runtime-mode extern path (pystachy.py:8015-8024, 10925-10945) behind an explicit marker, so existing programs keep their meaning. A pure-Python twin `py/ffi.py` (ctypes plus importlib) defines the boundary semantics: exact types, range checks and copies. The same file therefore prints the same under CPython, as LPython's @ccall does and as the `_rt` twin does for runtime.py. I prototyped the twin and checked it under CPython 3.13.

**(2) CPython calls Pystachy.** `pystachy ext mod.py` turns an ordinary annotated module into a Stable-ABI extension:
- Primary target: abi3t 3.15, through PEP 793 `PyModExport_<mod>` and PEP 820 PySlots. One `.abi3t.so` serves both GIL and free-threaded 3.15+.
- Secondary target: abi3 with a 3.12 floor.
- Each exported function gets a compiler-emitted METH_FASTCALL trampoline with a catch-all `pys_personality` landing pad, so no exception ever crosses a foreign frame.
- A cache-on-import hook (the `mojo.importer`/LPython `@lpython` model) serves the dev loop.

**(3) The boundary layer.** Per-program pieces (declares, trampolines, method and slot tables) are emitted in IR with only i64, double and ptr signatures. Fixed logic lives in a clang-compiled `pyrt.c` written against a checked-in Stable-ABI declarations header. There is no Python.h and no Python at build time, as pyo3-ffi does it. runtime.c gains about 85 inert lines of library mode:
- an idempotent init with no signals, setvbuf, argv or exit;
- a stack bottom per outermost entry;
- spill-and-record "park" records around call-outs, which save and restore xr/unw without TLS;
- a pin table scanned in mark_roots;
- an stdout hook.

**Tiers.** Pystachy→C and Pystachy→CPython use BOTH tiers with identical IR (one `-dlopen` on the lli line versus `-l` on the link). CPython→Pystachy is AOT only. There is no in-process JIT.

**Measured here.**
- CPython→Pystachy call: 15.5-16.4 ns on 3.15, 3.15t and 3.13, and abi3t is no slower than a version-specific build. A Python-level call is 17 ns and ctypes is 300+ ns.
- Pystachy→CPython vectorcall: 22 ns. A GC park adds 0.5-0.9 ns. Variadic PyObject_CallFunction costs 28.5 ns.
- Dev extension build: 130 ms. LTO release build: 470-600 ms. Cached import: 0.35 ms.

Everything is staged and pay-for-use. Only immutable values cross in v1; mutable containers cross only by explicit `@byvalue` copies. Opaque handles, classes and the typed-IR §7.4 zero-copy lowering come later.
jit_aot_answer:
**Pystachy → C: BOTH.** One IR `declare` serves both tiers.
- **JIT:** the driver appends `-dlopen=lib<x>.so` for each `@extern` library to the lli command at pystachy.py:16670. lli's -dlopen does dlopen(RTLD_LAZY|RTLD_GLOBAL), and LLJIT links process symbols by default (web-llvm). I verified crc32 from libz and cbrt from libm under lli-18 (stage2/sota-perf/e4/ext_c.ll).
- **AOT:** the driver appends `-l<x>` to the final clang link at pystachy.py:16653 (verified in the same file).
- **Where the JIT helps:** the edit-run loop. A warm `pystachy run` measured 53-60 ms with no link step, against 155 ms for `pystachy build`.
- **Where AOT helps:** shipping and start-up. A hello program starts in 1.5 ms AOT against 24 ms under lli, and only AOT does whole-program LTO with the runtime.
- **JIT constraint:** C code must come as shared objects, not `-extra-object` .o files, because native TLS in an extra object is silently wrong under lli-18 (web-llvm).

**Pystachy → CPython: BOTH** when Pystachy is the host process (embedding).
- **JIT:** `lli -dlopen=$PYSTACHY_PYLIB`, verified with libpython 3.13 and 3.15t (web-capi, spike-pys-to-py, web-llvm).
- **AOT:** link against $PYSTACHY_PYLIB, verified with 3.13 (spike-pys-to-py).
- **Inside an AOT extension:** Python symbols come from the host process, with no libpython link (PEP 513).
- **Cost:** interpreter init adds 12-16 ms in either tier.
- **Callbacks:** CPython calling back into Pystachy while Pystachy hosts also works in both tiers (web-llvm bidi test).

**CPython → Pystachy (CPython is the host): AOT only.**
- **Why:** CPython imports only shared objects, and `pystachy run` exec's lli as a separate process (pystachy.py:16670-16671).
- **Dev loop:** a compile-on-import cache.
  - The dev profile skips runtime LTO and links a cached runtime .o and pyrt.o: 129-136 ms cold, 0.35 ms on a cache hit. Code speed is unchanged (fib(25) 0.258 ms against 0.287 ms release); per call it is 18 against 14-15 ns.
  - Release builds use LTO: 470-600 ms.
- **Not an in-process ORC JIT.** It would cost 28.5 ms per process plus a 6-9 ms dlopen of a 117-123 MB libLLVM, 65 MiB RSS against 9 MiB, an ORC C API marked unstable, and a libgcc_s RTLD_GLOBAL preload (spike-py-to-pys, spike-pys-to-py, web-llvm). Its only gain is about 100 ms on the first-ever build of changed source.

directions.tier: Both: JIT (lli -dlopen) and AOT (-l at link), identical IR
directions.example:
```python
# crc.py
from ffi import extern, c_int, c_uint


@extern("z")
def crc32(crc: int, buf: bytes, n: c_uint) -> int: ...   # uLong crc32(uLong, const Bytef *, uInt)


@extern("m")
def cbrt(x: float) -> float: ...


@extern("c")
def strcmp(a: str, b: str) -> c_int: ...


data = b"hello world"
print(crc32(0, data, len(data)))   # 222957957
print(cbrt(27.0))
print(strcmp("a", "b"))           # -1
```

```sh
pystachy run crc.py                           # JIT: lli -dlopen=libz.so -dlopen=libm.so ...
pystachy build crc.py -o crc && ./crc         # AOT: ... -lz -lm
PYTHONPATH=$PYSTACHY_HOME/py python3 crc.py   # the oracle
```
directions.types_and_marshalling:
v1 lowers only to i64, double, ptr and i32. The first three are attribute-free on every LLVM target (web-llvm).

| Pystachy type | C type | lowering |
|---|---|---|
| int | int64_t | i64 |
| float | double | double |
| c_int / c_uint | int32_t / uint32_t | declared `signext i32` / `zeroext i32` as parameters; returned as plain i32, then sext/zext in IR; OverflowError on a narrowing argument, in compiled code and twin alike |
| str parameter | const char* | Str+8: NUL-terminated UTF-8 with no copy (repo-abi) |
| bytes parameter | const uint8_t* | same; the length goes in its own parameter |
| str or `str \| None` result | const char* | copied with pys_str; NULL gives None, or ValueError |
| Ptr | void* | an int-typed opaque handle, never dereferenced (Wasm-friendly) |
| None result | void | — |

c_int is required, not optional. Declaring `int strcmp()` as i64 returns 4294967295 instead of -1 on x86-64 in both tiers (verified in stage2/sota-perf/e4/wide2.ll). This resolves stage 1's split between "int only" (repo-abi) and "reject narrow ints" (web-llvm).

Rejected at compile time: bool, as today at 10931; structs by value; varargs; callbacks; and lists, dicts and classes.
directions.lifetimes:
The GC needs nothing new:
- A str or bytes argument stays live in the caller's frame, which the conservative scan covers. The heap is non-moving, so the pointer is valid for the whole call.
- In v1 C cannot call back, so no collection runs during the call.

C must copy anything it keeps past the call. This is Julia's GC-preserve rule, stated in docs/ffi.md.
- Returned char* data is copied immediately. Ownership stays with C, and v1 accepts only static or borrowed strings.
- Memory C owns travels as Ptr and is released through an explicit `@extern` free function.
- Nothing Pystachy owns is ever stored in C memory in v1, so no pins are needed.
directions.exceptions:
C never unwinds into Pystachy: extern calls carry no R effect and get no invoke. A Pystachy raise never reaches a C frame either: there are no callbacks in v1.

Later (stage 5), C callbacks get compiler-emitted trampolines. Each has a catch-all landing pad that stores the Exc and returns a status code (Numba's retcode convention). The raise is re-thrown after the C call returns. This avoids the measured failure modes of forced unwinding through foreign frames: a silent skip, or exit(1) (repo-abi).

C++ libraries must be wrapped behind extern "C" noexcept functions. A foreign exception passing Pystachy frames leaves unw/xr stale (repo-abi).
directions.threads_and_gil:
In standalone programs, all calls happen on the runtime's single thread; there is no GIL.

Inside an extension module, an extern call runs with the GIL held, as every C-API extension's plain C work does. A later `@extern(..., nogil=True)` could wrap the call in a park plus PyEval_SaveThread/RestoreThread (Stable ABI). Only then may other Python threads, including ones entering Pystachy, run during long C calls.

C code must not call Pystachy from its own threads (rejected by design in v1).

directions.tier: Both: JIT (lli -dlopen=$PYSTACHY_PYLIB) and AOT (link $PYSTACHY_PYLIB); inside an extension module the host provides the symbols
directions.mechanism:
`@pycall("module")` on a typed `...` stub, imported from `ffi` like `@extern`. The import and getattr run when the def statement executes during module init, which is when CPython runs the decorator. The callable is cached as a strong ref in a static.

Each call:
1. converts its arguments in IR through pyrt helpers;
2. calls PyObject_Vectorcall with PY_VECTORCALL_ARGUMENTS_OFFSET and a stack array (no tuple, no varargs);
3. converts the result with an exact type check;
4. Py_DecRefs every temporary.

E2 measured 22.2-22.7 ns per call on 3.15/3.15t, against 28-29 ns for PyObject_CallFunction("L").

Each call-out is a GC park: spill the registers with __builtin_unwind_init, then a noinline record. That costs 0.5-0.9 ns (E2). It is needed because Python code can switch the GIL to another thread that enters Pystachy (spike-py-to-pys segfault, web-gc 200/200).

Standalone programs embed CPython. The first @pycall binding runs Py_InitializeEx(0) if Py_IsInitialized() is false, and pys_finish runs Py_FinalizeEx. Both are Stable ABI.

The driver links libpython only when the program uses @pycall. It never runs python3, so the Python-free stage is safe. If PYSTACHY_PYLIB is unset, the result is file:line: error 'this program calls CPython; set PYSTACHY_PYLIB to libpython3.X.so'.

Effects are FXALL: Python code may raise, allocate or call back.
directions.example:
```python
# usejson.py
from ffi import pycall


@pycall("json")
def dumps(obj: dict[str, int]) -> str: ...


@pycall("statistics")
def median(data: list[float]) -> float: ...


counts: dict[str, int] = {"a": 1, "b": 2}
print(dumps(counts))           # {"a": 1, "b": 2}
print(median([3.0, 1.0, 2.0]))  # 2.0
```

```sh
export PYSTACHY_PYLIB=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpython3.13.so
pystachy run usejson.py                             # JIT: lli -dlopen=$PYSTACHY_PYLIB
pystachy build usejson.py -o usejson && ./usejson   # AOT: links $PYSTACHY_PYLIB
PYTHONPATH=$PYSTACHY_HOME/py python3 usejson.py     # the oracle
```
directions.runs_under_cpython: The twin's `ffi.pycall(module)` does getattr(importlib.import_module(module), name) at decoration time. The returned wrapper copies and type-checks arguments and result by annotation, with the same rules the compiled side uses. Containers are deep-copied in both runs, so aliasing is identical by construction. Verified under CPython 3.13: usejson.py prints {"a": 1, "b": 2} and 2.0 (stage2/sota-perf/twin).
directions.types_and_marshalling:
All values cross by value in v1:

| Pystachy | CPython | conversion |
|---|---|---|
| int | PyLong (exact; bool rejected) | PyLong_AsLongLong/FromLongLong (Stable ABI 3.2); OverflowError past 64 bits, matching checked int |
| float | PyFloat (exact) | PyFloat_AsDouble/FromDouble |
| bool | Py_True/Py_False | — |
| None | Py_None | Py_GetConstantBorrowed(0) in 3.13+, &_Py_NoneStruct for 3.12 |
| str | PyUnicode | in: PyUnicode_AsUTF8AndSize fast path, then one pys_str copy; surrogatepass fallback (spike-py-to-pys round-trips lone surrogates and NUL); out: PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8 with surrogatepass |
| bytes | PyBytes | one copy |
| tuple, `T \| None` | tuple, None or value | element-wise |
| list, dict, set | list, dict, set | deep copy using strong-ref getters (PyList_GetItemRef, PyDict_GetItemRef), never borrowed ones (PEP 733) |

Rejected in v1: class instances and Ptr. Stage 5 adds `ffi.PyObj` opaque handles.
directions.lifetimes:
In v1 every PyObject* is a temporary in the call thunk.
- Arguments are new references, decref'd after the call. The result is converted, then decref'd. The cached callable is held for the process.
- No PyObject* is ever stored in the Pystachy heap, so no finalizer is needed.

This matters because a wrapper that dies without a decref leaked 50,000 CPython blocks per 50,000 wrappers (spike-pys-to-py), and Pystachy's GC has no finalizers.

Stage 5 adds `ffi.PyObj`: an int-indexed handle table, not raw pointers, so it maps to Wasm externref tables later.
- Release is explicit through close() or `with`.
- A backstop is a post-mark sweep cloned from files_sweep (runtime.c:1815). It queues dead handles' decrefs and drains them at the next boundary crossing while the thread is attached, never inside collect(). This is the PyO3 reference pool / pythonnet Finalizer / PythonCall pattern.
- Cross-heap cycles are documented as leaks (as PEP 818 and JPype do) and counted in PYSTACHY_GC=stats.
directions.exceptions:
A NULL result triggers PyErr_GetRaisedException (Stable ABI 3.12, not the deprecated PyErr_Fetch Codon still uses). The exception maps into Pystachy's closed exception set:
- An exact builtin type goes to the same-named Pystachy kind.
- Any other class goes to its nearest builtin ancestor, so `except ValueError` catches json.JSONDecodeError exactly as in CPython.
- The message is str(exc). KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit(code) map to themselves.

The original exception object is kept as a pinned handle in the Exc (pys_exc_obj). If it propagates back out through an extension boundary, it is restored as the same object (the pythonnet 3.0 precedent). The raise uses the existing pys_raise path, so a try around a @pycall call is an invoke because of the R effect.
directions.threads_and_gil:
**Embedding.** The main thread holds the GIL after Py_InitializeEx, and Pystachy never detaches except inside Python's own blocking calls. Every call-out is a park, so a Python thread that gets the GIL and calls back into Pystachy collects with this thread's suspended range [park_top, bottom] as a root.

**Per-thread state without TLS.** The exception record xr and the unwind-action stack are saved into the park record and restored at unpark. That gives per-thread semantics without TLS in runtime.c, which also avoids lli-18's native-TLS trap for -extra-object (web-llvm).

**Inside an extension.** The same parks apply. Free threading is covered by the extension module's GIL policy (direction 3).

directions.tier: AOT only (extension module); dev loop through a compile-on-import cache
directions.example:
```python
# fastmath.py: an ordinary module; CPython can import it as source
# pystachy: ext
from ffi import byvalue


class TooBig(Exception):
    pass


def fib(n: int) -> int:
    if n > 90:
        raise TooBig("fib(" + str(n) + ") does not fit in 64 bits")
    a, b = 0, 1
    for _ in range(n):
        a, b = b, a + b
    return a


def shout(s: str) -> str:
    return s.upper() + "!"


@byvalue                       # the list crosses by copy, under CPython too
def total(xs: list[float]) -> float:
    t = 0.0
    for x in xs:
        t += x
    return t
```

```python
# app.py: plain CPython
import pystachy_import          # optional: compile on import, cached in __pycache__
import fastmath

print(fastmath.fib(90), fastmath.shout("hi"), fastmath.total([1.0, 2.5]))
try:
    fastmath.fib(91)
except fastmath.TooBig as e:
    print("caught", e)
```

```sh
pystachy ext fastmath.py -o fastmath.abi3t.so                 # release build for a wheel (cp315-abi3.abi3t)
pystachy ext fastmath.py --abi abi3 -o fastmath.abi3.so       # 3.12+ GIL builds
python3 app.py                                                # dev loop through the importer
PYSTACHY_IMPORT=off PYTHONPATH=$PYSTACHY_HOME/py python3 app.py   # the oracle: runs fastmath.py as source
```

Under CPython 3.13 the source run prints `2880067194370816120 HI! 3.5` and `caught fib(91) does not fit in 64 bits` (verified in stage2/sota-perf/twin). `pystachy check fastmath.py` parses it; today `run` rejects it with "module 'ffi' is not supported".
directions.runs_under_cpython:
The module is plain Python, so importing it without the hook, or with PYSTACHY_IMPORT=off, is the oracle.

The test harness runs the same driver script against the source module and against the built .so on 3.15, 3.15t, 3.13 and 3.12, and diffs stdout, stderr and status.

The twin's `byvalue` deep-copies and type-checks arguments and results by annotation. Container copies are therefore the semantics in both runs, not a hidden deviation. This keeps issue #4 §4's rule: mutable Python objects stay Python objects by default, and copies happen only when explicit.
directions.types_and_marshalling:
Types that cross in v1:
- int: exact PyLong; bool rejected. PyLong_AsLongLong gives OverflowError past 64 bits.
- float: exact PyFloat; an int raises TypeError 'expected float, got int', the compiler's own static rule.
- bool, None, str, bytes, `T | None`, and tuples of these.
- list, dict and set only under `@byvalue`: deep copy, using the existing dict accessors pys_dict_end/key/val (runtime.c:1508-1510) rather than the struct layout.
- Instances of user exception classes, through generated Python subclasses.

str crosses with one UTF-8 copy in each direction, with surrogatepass. Inside Pystachy, str keeps the documented byte semantics (docs/language.md:488-492; typed-ir.md:1132 'check or reject'). ASCII behaves exactly like CPython. A `--strict-str` option raises ValueError for non-ASCII at the boundary for callers who need exactness.

Keyword arguments are parsed against a parameter-name table in pyrt.c. Classes and handles come in stage 5 as heap types built with PyType_FromSpec, negative basicsize and PyObject_GetTypeData (3.12+). Zero-copy containers and buffers come in stage 6, through the typed-IR §7.4 lowering and PyObject_GetBuffer.

Measured costs:
- the full Pystachy trampoline: 14-15 ns per inc() call in release, 18 ns in dev (E3);
- the boundary alone: 15.5-16.4 ns for abi3t, abi3 and version-specific builds alike (E1);
- a raise across the boundary: about 0.8 µs (spike-py-to-pys).
directions.lifetimes:
In v1 only values cross, so Python never holds a Pystachy pointer.

Inside a call:
- The outermost entry's frame becomes the stack bottom. This fixes the measured SIGSEGV when the runtime was initialized in a deep frame (PyInit under importlib) and called from a shallower one.
- Module globals stay roots through @pys.roots.

Stage 5 adds two mechanisms:
- **Wrappers for Pystachy objects:** one wrapper per object through an address→wrapper map (the GC is non-moving, so `is` identity holds). Each wrapper holds an int pin slot from a free-list pin table that mark_roots scans; tp_dealloc unpins it. Without pins, capsule-held objects were measured as freed and reused.
- **Shutdown:** a free hook drains the decref queue while Py_IsFinalizing() is false.

Re-import does not rerun the runtime init (pys_init_lib is idempotent). A second exec of the same .so is refused with ImportError instead of resetting process-wide globals (spike-py-to-pys found that reset). The importer handles reload by building a new cache key.
directions.exceptions:
Every exported trampoline and the init are exception firewalls: invoke plus a catch-all pad under pys_personality. Nothing reaches uncaught() and its exit(), and the forced unwind (runtime.c:2319) never walks CPython frames. Unwinding through them was measured to leak one reference per crossing and to hit RecursionError after about 1,000 crossings (web-llvm).

The mapping:
- Builtin kinds go to the PyExc_* objects through a static table, not a builtins-dict lookup.
- User classes go to the per-module subclasses, exported as attributes, so `except fastmath.TooBig` works.
- SystemExit maps to SystemExit(code).
- KeyError carries its key, not str(key). The spike produced KeyError("'missing'").
- A Python exception that tunneled through compiled frames is restored as the original object.

In library mode, oom raises a MemoryError Exc preallocated at init instead of calling exit(1). A user __str__ that raises during conversion gets a nested pad. Ctrl-C stays CPython's, because pys_init_lib installs no SIGINT handler (spike-verified).
directions.threads_and_gil:
**GIL builds:** the GIL serializes Pystachy code. Parks around every call-out let other threads enter safely (spike: 3 of 3 runs passed with spans, exit 139 without).

**Free-threaded 3.15t:** a single abi3t binary loads. Py_mod_gil=USED re-enables the GIL with a RuntimeWarning (web-capi). The exec slot refuses import with ImportError if sys._is_gil_enabled() is False, which happens when PYTHON_GIL=0 or -Xgil=0 forces it off.

**Later (stage 7):** a world lock lets the module declare GIL_NOT_USED. Use PyCriticalSection_Begin/End (Limited 3.15) on a module-owned object, which is released when the thread detaches, i.e. at parks. This replaces web-gc's proposed PyMutex, which is not in the Limited API (web-capi).

**Subinterpreters:** NOT_SUPPORTED, since there is one world per process.

**Multiple Pystachy extensions:** each internalizes its own runtime with hidden symbols (RTLD_LOCAL loading), so their heaps and PYS_EXC handling never meet. Values cross only through Python.

abi_target:
**Primary: abi3t, CPython 3.15+** (PEP 803, Final 2026-03-30).
- Build: Py_TARGET_ABI3T=0x030F0000.
- Module definition: PEP 793 `PyModExport_<mod>` returning a PEP 820 PySlot array.
- Required Py_mod_abi slot with PyABIInfo {1, 0, flags STABLE|GIL|FREETHREADED = 7, build_version, abi_version 0x030F0000}.
- Other slots: Py_mod_name, Py_mod_methods with PySlot_STATIC, Py_mod_exec, Py_mod_gil=USED, Py_mod_multiple_interpreters=NOT_SUPPORTED.
- File and wheel: `.abi3t.so`, tag cp315-abi3.abi3t. It loads on 3.15+ with or without the GIL.
- Verified by web-capi as a pure-IR module, headerless and without libpython, on 3.15.0b4 and 3.15.0b4t. Final 3.15.0 shipped 2026-10-09 and has not been re-verified.

**Secondary: abi3 with a 3.12 floor.**
- Module definition: multi-phase `PyInit_<mod>` plus PyModuleDef and PyModuleDef_Init.
- The Py_mod_gil slot is emitted only for floor ≥ 3.13, because 3.12 rejects unknown slot IDs.
- File and wheel: `.abi3.so`, tag cp312-abi3, for GIL builds 3.12-3.15+.
- The floor is 3.12 because PyObject_Vectorcall, PyErr_GetRaisedException/SetRaisedException, PyType_FromMetaclass and PyObject_GetTypeData are all Stable ABI from 3.12. 3.13+ adds Py_GetConstantBorrowed, PyList_GetItemRef and Py_IsFinalizing; pyrt.c falls back to &_Py_NoneStruct and skips the shutdown decrefs on 3.12.

**Same IR for both ABIs.** The compiler emits identical IR. Only pyrt.c is compiled differently (-DPYRT_ABI3T, or -DPYRT_ABI3=0x030C0000), and the entry symbol name differs.

**Version-specific builds are rejected.** E1 measured the same METH_FASTCALL cost on 3.15 GIL: version-specific 15.5-25.1 ns (one noisy run), abi3 16.0-16.1 ns, abi3t 15.5-16.2 ns. On 3.15t: 16.3-16.4 ns either way. On 3.13: 15.7-16.0 ns either way. The boundary does few refcount operations, so abi3t's out-of-line Py_IncRef/Py_DecRef cost nothing measurable. That answers web-capi's open question for this workload.

**Embedding (Pystachy hosts CPython)** links a specific libpython3.X but calls only Stable-ABI functions plus Py_InitializeEx/Py_FinalizeEx, which are stable. PEP 741 config is not limited, so it is not used.

**Not targeted:** HPy (unmaintained since September 2026), PEP 809 abi2026 (Draft) and the PyNI draft (no PEP number). All CPython API use is confined to pyrt.c and pyabi.h, so a later switch touches two files.

invariants:
**CPython-or-compile-error contract.** Every `ffi` construct is valid Python. The twin py/ffi.py gives it exact CPython semantics, with the twin's checks as the spec, so the compiled side matches by construction: exact types, as the compiler's static 'expected float, got int' rule; OverflowError on 64-bit and c_int narrowing; deep copies for containers.
- Extension modules are ordinary modules: the oracle imports the source; tests diff a driver script's output against the .so.
- A public function, class or global that cannot cross is a file:line error, not a silent omission.
- The only deviations are the existing documented ones (64-bit int, byte str), now applied at the boundary.

**Three-stage fixed point.** The compiler uses no `ffi` itself. New Gen code runs only when a program imports `ffi` or under `ext`, so stage1 == stage2 == stage3 still holds for both pystachy.py and runtime.py, which is untouched.

**Python-free stage.** No Python.h and no python3 anywhere in a build:
- pyabi.h is checked in;
- libpython is located with PYSTACHY_PYLIB, never python3-config;
- `pystachy ext` builds extension modules with only clang and LLVM (pure-IR and headerless modules verified by web-capi).

Tests that need CPython (tests/ext, ffi_py_*) form a separate `ext-cpython` verify step that the nopy stage skips. The nopy stage can still build and run the libm/libz @extern tests.

**irsame and pay-for-use.** Programs that do not import `ffi` take none of the new branches, so their IR stays byte-identical. Run the corpus irsame on every step. runtime.c's additions are new functions plus guarded hooks; spike-py-to-pys showed 40 of 40 outputs byte-identical with its version.

**UBSan, gc-stress and the runtime checks.**
- pyrt.c is built with PYSTACHY_CFLAGS like runtime.c, so the UBSan step instruments it.
- Every ext and ffi test also runs under PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS=1, as both spikes did.
- A dedicated thread test exercises parks: a GIL-releasing callback while another thread enters, 100 of 100 runs.
- rt-abi is extended to check pyrt.c's pys_*/pyrt_* signatures against the compiler's declares.
- runtime-table checks the new RUNTIME entries.
- abi_check.sh pins the undefined symbols to the Stable ABI of the target version.

**Wasm GC.**
- Nothing enters runtime.py.
- Handles (Ptr, pins, PyObj) are ints indexing tables, never raw pointers in _rt, and map to externref tables later (the Pyodide/PEP 818 model).
- @extern with int, float or c_int lowers to a Wasm import (module = library, field = symbol); str externs are rejected on that target.
- The park, pin and handle machinery lives only in runtime.c and pyrt.c, i.e. the LLVM tier.
rejected_at_compile_time: An `@extern` or `@pycall` stub whose body is not exactly `...`, or that is a method, a nested def or a template (unannotated parameter or TypeVar).
`@extern` signatures that use bool. This keeps today's rule at pystachy.py:10931 ('the runtime ABI passes bools as int'): pass int or c_int.

`@extern` parameter or result types outside int, float, str, bytes (parameter only), `str | None` (result only), c_int, c_uint, Ptr and None (result only). This covers lists, dicts, sets, tuples, class instances and optionals. Structs by value, varargs and function-pointer callbacks have no spelling and are rejected too.
`*args`, `**kwargs` or default values in `@extern` stubs.
A non-literal library name in `@extern(...)`/`@pycall(...)`, or a non-ASCII C symbol.

The same C symbol declared twice with different signatures in one program, including across imported modules, or with a signature that differs from a RUNTIME raw symbol such as fabs, memchr or pys_*. llvm-link would otherwise accept the mismatch silently.
`ffi` imported from runtime.py (runtime mode keeps its pys_* extern rule, so _rt stays pointer-free).
Using an `@extern`/`@pycall` function as a value: functions as values are M3, the same existing error.
`@pycall` parameter or result types that are class instances or Ptr (opaque PyObj handles arrive in stage 5).
A program that uses `@pycall` with no PYSTACHY_PYLIB set, for `run`/`build` (an error naming the first @pycall line).

In `pystachy ext`: a public module-level function whose parameter or result type cannot cross. Mutable containers without `@byvalue` and class instances before stage 5 are errors naming the function, the parameter and the fix (`@byvalue`, a tuple, or a `_` prefix).
In `pystachy ext`: a public generic or template function (unannotated parameters), because CPython callers would expect it to exist.
In `pystachy ext`: a public non-exception class before stage 5, or a public mutable-container global (a copy would alias differently from CPython).
`@byvalue` on a function whose types cannot be deep-copied (class instances, Ptr, PyObj).
`pystachy ext` on a module whose name is not ASCII (PyModExportU_ punycode names are deferred).

Loading the runtime as bitcode takes 735 ms. A cached AOT .so imports in 0.35 ms and builds in 130 ms in the dev profile.

**Version-specific (non-Limited) extension builds:** E1 shows no call-overhead gain at this boundary (16 ns either way on 3.15, 3.15t and 3.13), while they need a build per CPython version and Python.h at build time.
**HPy:** declared unmaintained in September 2026. **PyNI:** a draft with no PEP number. **PEP 809 abi2026:** still Draft. Isolating the CPython API in pyrt.c and pyabi.h keeps a later switch cheap.

**Python.h-based glue:** it would require Python headers in builds and break Python-free extension builds. The Stable ABI is a binary contract that can be declared directly (pyo3-ffi does this; web-capi verified headerless modules).

**Emitting all CPython glue directly in IR:** verified on x86-64 Linux, but it hard-codes target C ABI details (int returns, Windows unsigned long, signext on riscv64/ppc64le) and different slot numbering for abi3 and abi3t in subset-compiler code. Keep only per-program tables and trampolines in IR.

**Header import in the compiler** (Zig @cImport, bindgen, Swift ClangImporter, libclang): a libclang- or Aro-sized dependency, i.e. a second toolchain. Zig itself moved translate-c out of the language. Typed stubs are the portable consensus (Codon, Julia @ccall, LPython @ccall, Shed Skin).
**ctypes or cffi as the CPython→Pystachy path:** 250-330 ns per call against about 15 ns for METH_FASTCALL, with no exception firewall.

**A bare `def f(...) -> T: ...` stub as the user extern form:** today it compiles to a RuntimeError, and it returns None under CPython. Reinterpreting it silently changes existing programs and breaks the contract.

**Letting Pystachy exceptions unwind through C or CPython frames** (a C-unwind style ABI): measured to leak one reference per crossing and to raise RecursionError after about 1,000 crossings. Without unwind tables it exits the process.

**Implicit container copies at the extension boundary** (Shed Skin, Codon): this contradicts issue #4 §4 and the contract. Copies happen only through explicit `@byvalue`, whose twin copies under CPython too.

**Waiting for the typed-IR §7.4 lowering before shipping anything:** it is blocked on step 16, about 58k raw ops, and recoverable elaboration. The wrapper-style extension ships now behind the same ABI and pyrt.c, and §7.4 later replaces its copies.

**A shared system-wide libpystachy runtime .so:** the runtime calls program-defined pys_obj_eq, pys_obj_cmp and pys_obj_repr, and sharing it loses runtime inlining. Use one internalized runtime per extension, and later one per package (mypyc/Cython model).
**Whole-stack scanning from __libc_stack_end:** it covers the main thread only and scans all of CPython's stack. Use a per-entry bottom plus park records.
**TLS in runtime.c for per-thread state:** native TLS in an -extra-object is silently wrong under lli-18. Park records save and restore xr/unw instead.

**Boehm-style finalizers or `__del__` to release PyObjects:** Pystachy's GC has no finalizers, and Boehm finalizers cannot reclaim cycles anyway. Use explicit close() with a sweep-queue backstop drained outside collect().
**PyMutex as the free-threading world lock** (web-gc's v2): it is not in the Limited API, so abi3t cannot use it. Use PyCriticalSection (Limited 3.15).
**Variadic CPython calls** (PyObject_CallFunction, Py_BuildValue, PyArg_ParseTuple): 28.5 ns against 22.2 ns for vectorcall (E2), and PEP 733 calls varargs hard for non-C frontends.
**dlopen and dlsym of libpython in v1** (the Codon CODON_PYTHON model): more code than lli -dlopen or a link flag. Defer it to when relocatable embedding binaries are needed.
risks: The str boundary: Pystachy's byte-indexed UTF-8 str reaches Python callers. len, indexing and case mapping of non-ASCII text differ from CPython; Codon 0.20 abandoned its UTF-8-bytes str for this reason. This is mitigated, not removed: ASCII is exact, the deviation is documented, and `--strict-str` rejects non-ASCII at the boundary.

abi3t was verified only on 3.15.0b4 and 3.15.0b4t from python-build-standalone. 3.15.0 final (2026-10-09) needs re-verification: Py_mod_methods requiring PySlot_STATIC, PyABIInfo build_version handling, the slot IDs.

Free-threaded users get the GIL re-enabled with a RuntimeWarning, and an ImportError under PYTHON_GIL=0, until S7. The PyCriticalSection world lock is untested: critical sections may be suspended at any detach, so every C-API call that can detach must be a park point.

Output ordering. ext mode routes Pystachy's print through sys.stdout.write, which changes buffering and performance for print-heavy code. In embedding mode, replacing sys.stdout with a TextIOWrapper over Pystachy's stream could differ in edge attributes such as `sys.stdout.buffer` or isatty.

Remaining exit paths in library mode: oom inside collect() (mitigated by the preallocated MemoryError, but collect() cannot raise mid-sweep), stack overflow (the recursion limit is only recorded), and kbint_exit. Any of them would kill the host interpreter.
Re-import and reload semantics with process-global module state. A second exec is refused; reload works only by rebuilding under a new cache key, which leaks the old runtime instance.

Two Pystachy extensions in one process have separate heaps and runtimes. Objects cross between them only by value through Python, which may surprise users who expect shared classes. A per-package shared runtime (mypyc model) is later work.

Performance granularity: on 3.15 a Python-level call costs 17 ns against about 15 ns across the boundary (E1). Fine-grained calls gain nothing, and str or container copies add tens of ns each. Users must export coarse-grained functions, and the eligibility report should flag hot small functions. CPython's own JIT may narrow the gap further.

Effects: @pycall callees are FXALL, which blocks the listget and dictfuse optimizations around them. Treating @extern as effect {I} assumes C neither retains str pointers past the call nor calls back; a violation is a use-after-free under GC.
Cross-heap reference cycles (stage 5 PyObj ↔ wrapper) leak by design until a cross-component tracer exists, an estimated +150-300 lines.
Only x86-64 Linux was tested. macOS (-undefined dynamic_lookup, compact unwind), Windows (python3.dll, __imp_ data, no Itanium forced unwind under MSVC) and AArch64 Linux are unverified.
C++ libraries throwing through Pystachy frames, or pybind11 frames between Pystachy segments, leave unw/xr stale. @extern targets must be C or noexcept shims.

pyabi.h prototypes can drift from CPython's. Mitigations: generate them from Misc/stable_abi.toml, check them with nm in CI, and optionally compile pyrt.c against the real Python.h in the ext-cpython step.
The Python-free CI rule: the ext and @pycall tests need python3 and libpython, so they live in a separate verify step. A regression there is invisible to the nopy stage.
The LLVM pin: Pystachy targets LLVM 18. Moving past LLVM 23 requires changing float literal emission (pystachy.py:6006-6021), and lli flag behaviour must be rechecked with that toolchain.
